feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/communications CV with credible progression, relevant public-sector scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads clearly and professionally, but impact is diluted by repetition, limited quantified outcomes beyond traffic scale, and a slightly overstuffed structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo into director-level ownership of web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.  
- Good credibility signals: named platforms/tools, large-scale website migration, audience/traffic figures, and concrete recent projects.  
- Writing is polished and mostly error-free, with concise, professional phrasing and consistent action-led bullets.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and project/footer content; consolidate to create a tighter, more executive-level CV.  
- Add more outcome metrics: team size, budget, engagement lifts, email performance, efficiency gains, search improvements, campaign results, or revenue/member impact.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; consider consistent capitalization for “organization-wide”; “French (A2/Learning)” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” Also consider whether “Ranked among the top public universities...” adds value in Education.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and relevant scope, but it’s slightly dense and repeats language already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening it with a clearer value proposition and a few concrete anchors will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for public-sector and mission-driven organizations. Combines digital strategy, governance, analytics, editorial operations, and multimedia production to improve publishing efficiency, audience reach, and user experience.”
- Add 1 concrete scale marker from recent work if space allows, e.g. “10,000+ page website” or “3.5M annual page views,” to make the intro more credible.
- Replace “AI-enabled user experiences” with a more specific phrase such as “AI-enabled search and content discovery.”
- Use parallel structure: “web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled…” and the long capability list overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Senior digital leader” is somewhat redundant with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into sharper, less repetitive capability areas with more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, cleaner labels and keep all items in a consistent noun-phrase style.
- Emphasize highest-value strengths most supported by recent roles: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and platform/workflow integration.
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space is tight, replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” and “communications operations” with “communications leadership” for more impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming either this block or the Topline Skills categories.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is somewhat redundant with the public-sector emphasis already established elsewhere.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and making the footer feel more selective will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” to reinforce recency and purpose.
- Shorten each item to one crisp outcome-focused line; e.g., “Created an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure: start each project with a strong verb and avoid stacking too many features in one sentence.
- Change “10×20-foot” to “10 x 20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely repeat achievements already described in the current freelance role.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with NACo video/studio accomplishments; keep only if it adds distinct scope or channel strategy.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and add outcomes or scale to distinguish it from your NACo entries.

Suggested edit
- Replace the generic opener with a sharper scope statement: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, Drupal platform improvement, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like “Built,” “Led,” “Developed,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable context where possible: number of sites/pages/users, team/stakeholder groups supported, workflow time saved, publishing efficiency gained, search accuracy/adoption, or campaign/toolkit usage.
- Example rewrite: “Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, creating modular microsites, reusable content components, and member toolkits while improving publishing consistency and speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, and cross-channel best practices” overlaps with NACo Director/Associate Director bullets; keep only if you can show a distinct result or newer technical scope.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections; emphasize business impact, not just capabilities.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good platform detail and scale. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation wins, and add clearer outcomes for channels, analytics, and governance.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize highest-impact achievements first: website migration, analytics modernization, video studio, then channel leadership/governance.
- Add outcome language where possible: site performance, publishing efficiency, reporting speed, campaign capacity, production cost savings, engagement growth, or stakeholder adoption.
- Tighten channel bullet to avoid vague audience language: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching county officials nationwide” unless you can add open rates, subscriber growth, engagement, or conversions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on building the studio and scaling in-house production capacity.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” appears across multiple NACo roles; here, emphasize enterprise governance and cross-department systems, not day-to-day coordination.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process gains achieved before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging during a period of organizational growth.”
- Tighten bullets to action + outcome: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more impact-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with ownership and outcome: “Built more consistent publishing workflows and cross-team editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Reframe for specificity and seniority:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization  
- Editorial governance & cross-functional content operations  
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications  
- Audience-centered campaign and content planning
- Replace “Multi-channel communications leadership” with something more concrete like “Cross-channel communications strategy” or “Integrated web, email, social & multimedia planning.”
- Consider dropping one generic line and keeping this to 4 bullets max; “audience-focused content planning” is the weakest/most generic.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable scale for experience bullets rather than skills (e.g., 10,000+ page Drupal migration, 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems/governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already strongly established in the summary and NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. Make it more strategic and recent by emphasizing modernization, implementation, and AI/search outcomes rather than listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, not software-led: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “CMS modernization & front-end implementation” instead of separate platform/code fragments
- Group technical skills into outcomes-oriented clusters: “API integrations, workflow automation, and Airtable-based systems”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization & front-end implementation • HTML, CSS, JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the technical section carry the full tool list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” overlaps with current consulting work; keep it brief here since the experience entry already gives stronger context.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for recent leadership roles, but the item reads like a raw keyword list. Tighten it into capability-led phrasing that signals business value, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g.: “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic terms with stronger phrasing: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” instead of “Leadership reporting”
- Clarify scope of analysis: “SEO, UX and web performance analysis” if accurate; this is broader and more strategic than “SEO and performance analysis”
- Possible rewrite: “Digital analytics & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity; KPI framework development; executive dashboarding; SEO, UX and web performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure; keep this skills item concise and avoid repeating impact claims here.
- If space is tight, consider dropping one dashboard tool here since both Looker Studio and Power BI already appear in recent experience context.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more specific to recent, higher-value capabilities and tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia, Studio & Live Event Production**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webinar production • PTZ camera and studio systems • Hybrid/virtual event delivery • Post-production editing**
- If accurate, add scale/complexity instead of generic terms: **Multi-camera livestreams • In-house studio buildout/operations**
- Keep only 5 items max and use parallel noun phrases; avoid broad wording like “video production and editing” if you can be more distinctive.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Core Competencies: **“Multimedia & live event production.”** Consider shortening one or removing the duplicate phrase there.
- “Studio operations” and event production are already evidenced in the 2022–2024 NACo role; don’t repeat the same wording verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent experience is strongly Drupal-led, this item should emphasize depth/relevance or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise CMS, migrations, modular content)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms** for clearer scope and less generic phrasing.
- If you want more impact, swap the weakest/least relevant platform for a stronger recent capability already evidenced elsewhere, but only if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the detailed version in one place only.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so this item should stay concise rather than repeat broad claims.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it tighter, more current, and framed around implementation strengths rather than basic languages.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Replace with: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses version-specific naming; they add little value at this level.
- If space allows, add one short qualifier tied to recent work, e.g., “for Drupal-based sites, campaign microsites, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider keeping detailed tools here and trimming overlapping terms from Topline Skills, or vice versa, to avoid repetition.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped, purpose-led categories: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”
- Put the strongest differentiators first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira; move common collaboration tools (Slack, Teams) to the end or remove.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” for more precision and stronger alignment with your recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating identical phrasing.
- Slack and Teams are very common and low-signal unless they support a stronger systems narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and undersells your email leadership. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise communications systems, frame these as platforms you’ve administered or used to run member communications.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are your strongest/current tools; otherwise order by recency and depth of use.
- If space allows, add light context: **Email marketing, newsletter operations, audience journeys, and member engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Use consistent naming/capitalization; “Customer Insights / Journeys” may be cleaner as **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- If Higher Logic or Dynamics 365 were central in recent roles, consider reflecting one of them in a recent experience bullet for stronger credibility.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this line is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it to platforms/methods and make the optimization angle more precise.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis** to keep this item tool/method-focused rather than broad marketing jargon.
- Change **Dashboarding** to **KPI/dashboard reporting** or **executive reporting** for clearer business value.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to outcomes in recent roles instead of here (e.g., analytics infrastructure, reporting adoption, decision-making improvements).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this one strictly tools-based.
- **Looker Studio** and **Power BI** already signal dashboarding/reporting, so “Dashboarding” is partially redundant.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and team-building impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving coordination across web, email, social and video.”
- Add specific scope/results if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, email/social performance, or workflow time saved.
- Tighten the second sentence around execution: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and coached a digital media associate on day-to-day publishing and production.”
- If metrics exist, replace “high-impact” with evidence: “produced X livestreams/year,” “launched weekly video series,” “supported Y% traffic growth,” etc.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the standout achievement and keep the rest tightly scoped to innovation/research support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; translated findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Remove vague wording like “contributed to” and “materials”; use stronger verbs such as “developed,” “produced,” or “supported.”
- If possible, add one metric or scope detail: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or types/volume of projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production, which is covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t repeat video/multimedia leadership language that belongs to the 2015–2024 positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tightening it to named tools plus a clearer production scope will feel more senior and avoid repeating broader multimedia claims already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape as tool-focused: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast editing/production • Livestream studio operations”
